title: Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update for Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation
claim: Handling each incoming dataset separately makes storage and training cost grow with every addition; one continually updated compact set keeps cost fixed.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right time arrow, red expanding vs blue fixed storage
description: Two stacked panels, (a) and (b), separated by a dashed line. Each has a green time arrow along the top. Below the arrow are four real dog-image datasets in different domains: photos, colorful paintings, cartoons and line sketches. Each dataset feeds a 'Storage' box that opens into a distilled-dataset tile. In (a), each domain adds a new stack of distilled images. The tiles and storage boxes shift from pale pink to saturated red, and the labels 'expansive' and 'slow' sit next to a small neural network. In (b), one fixed-size set of distilled images is updated step by step. Blue arrows link the tiles, the tiles stay light blue, and the labels read 'compact' and 'fast'. The red-versus-blue contrast and the growing stacks draw the eye first.
caption: Comparison of (a) existing Dataset Distillation and (b) the proposed Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation. (a) DD considers per-dataset distillation, which increases storage and training costs depending on the number of datasets. (b) DIDD maintains a fixed-size synthetic dataset over time, thereby keeping storage and training costs comparable to those of a single dataset.
abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) attempts to construct a compact synthetic dataset that serves as a proxy for a large real dataset under a fixed storage budget, thereby reducing the storage burden and training costs. Prior works assume the full dataset is available upfront which is distilled at once, although real datasets are collected incrementally over time in practice. To alleviate this gap, we introduce a new problem setting, Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation , that continually distills datasets from different domains into a single synthetic dataset. The conventional DD sequentially processes arriving datasets in order, overwriting the old knowledge with new one, causing catastrophic forgetting problem. To overcome this drawback, we propose Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update strategy that adjusts the per-sample update rates for synthetic dataset while balancing the stability-plasticity trade-off. Specifically, we design a bi-level optimization method based on meta-learning framework to estimate the optimal update rates, which allows each sample to focus on either stability or plasticity, thereby striking a balance between them. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively mitigates the catastrophic forgetting and achieves superior performance of DD across continually incoming datasets compared with existing methods.
